sections.h2: Where is the Graham County Recorder's Office and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Graham County Recorder is on the second floor of the Graham County General Services Building, 921 Thatcher Boulevard, Safford, AZ 85546. The office is open Monday through Thursday from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., and e-recordings are accepted through 5 p.m. on Friday. Holidays are excluded.

  • Phone: 928-428-3560.
  • Toll free: 888-428-3252.
  • Fax: 928-428-8828.
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 747, Safford, AZ 85548.

The Recorder keeps the county's property records and voter registration records. A seller in Graham County deals with the office when a deed, deed of trust release or similar paper has to be placed in the permanent public record, usually through the title or escrow company handling the sale.

sections.h2: What does the Graham County Recorder require before it will record a deed?
sections.html:
A deed has to meet the form rules in A.R.S. 11-480, and a document that fails any of them may be rejected when it is presented. Graham County publishes the same checklist on its Recording Requirements page.

RequirementRuleSource
CaptionA title or caption that briefly states what the document isA.R.S. 11-480; Graham County Recorder
Original and legibleAn original or certified copy clear enough to make certified copiesA.R.S. 11-480; Graham County Recorder
SignaturesOriginal signatures unless the law provides otherwiseA.R.S. 11-480; Graham County Recorder
Size and printNo larger than 8.5 by 14 inches, with type no smaller than 10 pointA.R.S. 11-480; Graham County Recorder
MarginsHalf an inch on the sides and bottom; a 2-inch top margin on page oneA.R.S. 11-480; Graham County Recorder
Changes to an earlier documentState the recording date and the docket and page or sequence number being modifiedA.R.S. 11-480(D)

The top margin of the first page is reserved for recording information. The left three and one-half inches may carry the name and return address of the person requesting recording. The county recorder does not provide forms. Forms come from office supply stores or title companies, and the office follows instructions from the Graham County Attorney not to give legal advice.

sections.h2: Do you need an Affidavit of Property Value to record a deed in Graham County?
sections.html:
Yes, unless the transfer is exempt. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires each deed that transfers title, and any contract about the sale of real property, to carry an affidavit signed by the buyer and seller or their agents. The county recorder must refuse to record the deed if the affidavit is incomplete and no exemption is noted.

The affidavit asks for the following:

  • Names, mailing addresses and phone numbers of the buyer and seller, and the address for the tax statement.
  • The legal description, the situs address and the assessor's parcel number.
  • The date of sale and the total consideration, including the down payment and the type of financing.
  • The relationship between the parties, and whether a residence will be owner-occupied or rented.

Exempt transfers must show the exemption on the face of the document. A.R.S. 11-1134 lists them, including a deed of gift, a quitclaim deed for no money consideration, a conveyance under a court order, and a transfer for nominal consideration between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings. Graham County says the Arizona Department of Revenue exemption number must accompany an exempt deed at the time of recording. A deed submitted with an incomplete affidavit or a missing one is returned to the submitter.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Graham County?
sections.html:
The state sets the base recording charge at $30 per instrument under A.R.S. 11-475. The same section sets $15 per instrument for papers where the United States, the state or a political subdivision is a party and requests the recording. Those figures include the amount charged under section 11-475.01.

Copies are priced by statute too: $1 for each page of a certified copy, plus $3 for attaching the recorder's certificate and seal. The county lists its fee rates on its Recording Information page, and the Recorder's phone number is the quickest way to confirm the total for a document with several pages or extra indexing.

On the question of transfer taxes, Article 9, Section 24 of the Arizona Constitution bars any new tax, fee or stamp requirement on conveying real property interests, with an exception for charges that existed on December 31, 2007. Ask your title company to show the recording charges on the settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: How can you record electronically or search records in Graham County?
sections.html:
Graham County offers an e-recording page, a digital recording account application and a list of e-recording providers, and a title company will normally handle submission for a sale. The office's document search lets anyone run searches of recorded documents through its Recorder web page.

The county also runs a free Recording Notification service. It watches documents recorded with the Recorder's office and alerts subscribers when something is recorded. That helps an owner spot a recording that does not belong on the property, such as a fraudulent deed. If you receive an alert and think you are a victim of fraud, the Recorder's page directs you to local law enforcement. The Recorder's page also takes requests for copies of death certificates and military discharge (DD-214) forms.

sections.h2: What should a Graham County seller prepare before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Have the deed carry original signatures, follow the margins above, and come with a completed affidavit or exemption code. Your title company usually prepares these papers, and this checklist helps you review them:

  • Confirm the assessor's parcel number matches the one on your tax bill.
  • Check that the full legal description appears, since the affidavit requires it.
  • Ask whether the deed is recorded by mail, in person or electronically, and when the recording number will be available.
  • Keep the recording number once it is issued, since a certified copy can be requested later if the original is lost.

Property tax runs on a separate track. The Graham County Treasurer can confirm what is owed on the parcel at 928-428-3440, and statements usually reach a new owner's name about a year after recording.

A titled mobile home is a separate case. Graham County bills it as personal property, and the tax record changes only when a new title is issued in the buyer's name. Signing the back of the old title does not update the roll, so finish the title transfer as well as the deed.

sections.h2: What is Graham County like for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Graham County, in southeastern Arizona, covers 4,641 square miles and was created on March 10, 1881. Safford is the county seat and its largest city, and Thatcher and Pima are the incorporated towns. Eastern Arizona College and the Mount Graham International Observatory are two of the larger institutions, and part of the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation lies inside the county.

The Census Bureau estimates the 2025 population at 40,157, with 14,645 housing units. Owners live in 73.1 percent of occupied homes, the median owner-occupied home was valued at $212,000 for 2020 through 2024, and median gross rent was $935. The county grew 4.2 percent between April 2020 and July 2025.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Graham County?
faqs.a: State law sets $30 per instrument for most papers under A.R.S. 11-475, or $15 when a government body is the party requesting recording. Call 928-428-3560 to confirm the total for a long document.

faqs.q: What are the Graham County Recorder's hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Thursday from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., excluding holidays, and takes e-recordings through 5 p.m. on Friday.

faqs.q: Does Graham County require an Affidavit of Property Value?
faqs.a: Yes, for deeds that transfer title, unless an exemption applies under A.R.S. 11-1134. An incomplete or missing affidavit leads the Recorder to return the document.

faqs.q: Can the Graham County Recorder help me prepare a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not provide forms and does not give legal advice, so use a title company or attorney. Forms are available at office supply stores or from title companies.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax in Graham County?
faqs.a: The Arizona Constitution bars any new tax or fee on conveying real property, except charges that existed on December 31, 2007. Ask your title company to list the recording and closing charges before you sign.
